[Chris Holmes][chris], founder of the Cloud-Native Geospatial Foundation and working at Planet, has 
published an interesting and personal account of how Portolan, the serverless SDI[^sdi] has come to be:
*"[A personal introduction to Portolan][article]"*. 

![A Portolan instance showing Dutch data (source: Chris Holmes)](portolan-nl-data-preview.gif "A Portolan instance showing Dutch data (source: Chris Holmes)")

The article touches on Chris's early work on GeoServer, on cloud-native formats such as 
GeoParquet[^geoparquet], COG[^cog], and Zarr[^zarr], and respective tooling, and finally on 
Portolan, a project to enable serverless SDIs that share cloud-native geodata broadly, in a 
human-friendly and AI-enabled form. 

From the [article][article]:

> So my more ‘modest’ hope for Portolan is that it greatly accelerates the adoption of CNG formats 
by the geospatial industry, and the standard way to share geospatial information becomes to put a
GeoParquet, COG, COPC[^copc] or Zarr in a bucket and include the appropriate `catalog.json`/`readme`/`agents.md`
file. [...]
>
> But the bigger goal I have for Portolan is to realize the vision of all the Spatial Data 
Infrastructure dreams of the past – to finally make the world’s fundamental geospatial information 
available and accessible to all. I believe this is now a tractable problem that can be solved, by 
leveraging AI in a couple of key ways.

[Recommended reading][article] if you are interested in SDIs, or even operate one.


[chris]: https://www.linkedin.com/in/opencholmes
[article]: https://9eo.org/blog/a-personal-introduction-to-portolan/

[^sdi]: Spatial Data Infrastructure: a framework of technologies, policies, and standards that 
enables the discovery, access, and sharing of geospatial data.
[^geoparquet]: [GeoParquet](https://geoparquet.org/) is an open-source specification that adds 
interoperable geospatial types to [Parquet](https://parquet.apache.org/), enabling efficient storage 
and columnar access of vector geodata.
[^cog]: Cloud-optimized GeoTIFF
[^zarr]: [Zarr](https://zarr.dev/) is an open, cloud-native format for storing large, chunked, 
N-dimensional arrays, commonly used for gridded and multi-dimensional Earth observation data.
[^copc]: Cloud-optimized point cloud
